cells.quote: Global teamwork performance improved in ten studies [23–29, 31, 32, 37]. result.effect: Approximately 16% reduction in total resuscitation time; no pooled effect size for protocol adherence

cells.quote: Evidence for clinical or process outcomes was limited but generally favourable in single-centre studies, including shorter resuscitation times and improved protocol adherence; no study reported effects on mortality or complication rates, and the certainty of evidence for these outcomes was rated as low to very low.
cells.note: Clinical/process evidence was based on a small number of studies and had low to very low certainty.

O.outcome_detail: Teamwork behavior among ICU professionals

cells.quote: Ten studies assessed teamwork behaviors. In nine of them, which had a before and after design, NTS training led to an increase in teamwork behavior, both in self-assessments [35, 37, 38, 40] and through direct observations tools [36, 39, 42, 45, 46], however with a low certainty of evidence. In the RCT by Jonsson et al. [47], there was little difference in teamwork behavior between control and intervention group after the training, with a moderate certainty of evidence.
cells.note: Narrative synthesis; pooled evidence was methodologically heterogeneous and included mostly uncontrolled before-and-after studies.

O.outcome_detail: Situational-awareness behavior among ICU professionals

cells.quote: Four of them showed increased scores using self-reported instruments [38] and external observations [39, 42, 46], however with a low or very low certainty of evidence. The studies of Jonsson et al. [47]. and Kemper et al. [48] found no significant differences in self-reported situational awareness assessments after training, both with a moderate level of certainty.
cells.note: The review reports improvement in some before-and-after studies but no significant differences in the controlled studies.

O.outcome_detail: Leadership behavior among ICU professionals

cells.quote: Leadership behaviors were assessed in six studies [36, 38–40, 42, 45]. In the study by Anderson et al. [36], there was a significant increase in the team’s leadership behavior after the intervention. The studies by Haerkens et al. [41], Guérin et al. [42], and Sawyer et al. [45] also showed a significant increase in leadership behavior after training, however with very low certainty of evidence. In contrast, Jonsson et al. [47] found little difference in leadership behavior between the intervention and control groups, with moderate certainty of evidence.
cells.note: Narrative synthesis with mixed study designs and low or moderate certainty depending on the comparison.

O.outcome_detail: Communication behavior among ICU professionals

cells.quote: In five before-and-after studies, communcation improved signicantly in self-assessments [38, 40] and through direct observation [39, 42, 45]. Even so, the improvement varieted considerably among the studies, with very low certainty of evidence. In the quasi-experimental study by Kemper et al. [48], no significant difference was found in communication behaviors between the intervention and control groups, with very low certainty of evidence.
